svg.text: talk.01 · v0.3 study · CONTROLS ABOVE, ONE BIG PICKUP BELOW
TE's layout turned upside down · a round hole under a square cover plate (a circle inside a square) · key upper-left, wheel top-right
TENTATIVE · NOT A FINAL DESIGN
front views at 10 mm = 45 px
A LINES
teal plate, horizontal slots · skin SAND
· Lines are the most 'old radio' pattern; the
engraved lines carry on across the plate, so
the round hole reads as cut through a grille.
· Risk: with only the circle slotted, the plate
corners are plain; keep or drop the engraved
lines? (open)
B SLOTS
dark plate, tall slots · skin POPPY
· The strongest contrast: a dark speaker panel
with a pale ring. The rainbow band separates
controls from pickup.
· Risk: the dark plate is heavy next to the
cream upper part; the plate may be the colour
instead.
C DOTS
colour block above, ring of holes · skin SAND
· Keeps the colour block of F1 as the control
zone and puts the big dotted circle below it:
nearest to the F3 idea.
· Risk: dots are the easiest to print but the
least 'radio'; the tick ring does the radio
work.
THE PLATE OVER THE HOLE (section, a sketch)
front of the body at the top
cover plate (printed)
standoffs: 1.5 mm gap
fine mesh or felt
wall with round hole
MEMS mic, port to hole
What this changes, honestly:
· the big circle is mostly STYLE. The microphone needs only a tiny
port (about 1 mm); the big hole just has to leave a clear air
path to it.
· so the plate pattern can be whatever looks right, if the mesh
and the gap do not block the air. That is cheap to test: print
the plate and record with and without it.
· no claim about sound is made here. Nothing has been recorded or
measured.
· lower pickup: when it leans back on its stand the mic sits close
to the desk. Keep it off the desk by the stand's height; check
for desk and key-tap noise.
· F1 note: its slim strip made the pickup small; the upper/lower
split gives the pickup roughly half the face.
